title: esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix — DeepSeek-native AI coding agent for your terminal. Engineered around prefix-cache stability — leave it running.
content:
English · 简体中文 · Guide · ACP · Extensions · Spec · Website · Discord
Open source · MIT · a single Go binary
One local engine, four ways in — terminal, desktop app, browser, or your editor over ACP. Plan mode, permissions, a workspace sandbox and per-turn checkpoints keep a long autonomous run something you can still read and undo.
logo-animation.mp4
Important
Community · 加入社区 — bilingual Discord for setup help (#help / #求助), workflow showcases, and feature ideas. → https://discord.gg/XF78rEME2D
- Config-driven. Providers, the agent, enabled tools, and plugins are all
declared in reasonix.toml . No hardcoded models.
- Multi-model & composable. DeepSeek ships as a preset; any OpenAI-compatible endpoint is a config entry, not new code. Optionally run two models together (executor + planner) in separate, cache-stable sessions.
- Plugin-driven. MCP servers contribute tools, prompts, and resources; Extension Protocol v1 sidecars can also intercept runtime events, contribute Providers and structured UI, and ship versioned plugin packages.
- Cache-aware context maintenance. Startup injects a small stable environment summary, stale tool output is snipped/pruned before summary compaction, and the built-in tool schema contract is documented for regression review.
- Zero-friction distribution. CGO_ENABLED=0 single binary; cross-compile
to six targets with one command. The result is a fully self-contained static
binary — nothing to install on the target machine beyond the binary itself.
Choose the path that matches how you want to use Reasonix. The CLI/TUI, desktop app, and VS Code extension all use the same local Reasonix engine.
Install the native binary through npm on any supported platform, or use Homebrew on macOS:
npm i -g reasonix                  # any OS; pulls the prebuilt native binary
brew install esengine/reasonix/reasonix   # macOS
Prebuilt archives (darwin|linux|windows × amd64|arm64) and SHA256SUMS are on
every GitHub release.
Use the official download page for the latest desktop build.
Windows installers are code-signed through SignPath.io with a free certificate provided by the SignPath Foundation.
Complete Path A first. The extension does not bundle the CLI; it starts your
local reasonix acp backend and adds native chat, editor context, tool-call
approvals, model selection, and workspace sessions.
- VS Code: install from Visual Studio Marketplace
- VSCodium / Eclipse Theia: install from Open VSX Registry
- Extension ID: SivanLiu.reasonix-agent · source and usage guide
Clone the repository first:
git clone https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix.git
cd DeepSeek-Reasonix
The CLI build requires Go 1.26+. The module pins a toolchain directive;
keep GOTOOLCHAIN=auto so Go downloads the pinned toolchain, or install it.
make build      # -> bin/reasonix(.exe)
make cross      # -> dist/ (darwin|linux|windows × amd64|arm64)
The desktop build additionally requires Node 24+ and pnpm 10
(npm install -g pnpm@10) for the frontend and the Electron shell:
scripts/desktop-build.sh darwin/arm64 v0.0.0-dev   # one platform per run
No platform webview dependencies are needed — the shell ships its own Chromium. See the desktop build guide.
These commands are for the CLI/TUI installed through Path A:
reasonix setup                      # configure a provider and model
reasonix                            # start an interactive session
reasonix run "implement the TODOs in main.go"
In an interactive session, run /init when you want Reasonix to create project
instructions.
Download the installer for your platform from the official download page, install and launch Reasonix, then configure a provider and model in the app. The CLI commands above are not required for the desktop app.
For advanced CLI usage and configuration, see the CLI reference, Guide, and configuration paths.

report.summary: DeepSeek-Reasonix is an MIT-licensed, single-binary terminal coding agent built around prefix-cache stability, letting developers run long autonomous DeepSeek sessions they can read and undo.
report.background: Terminal-native AI coding agents have moved from novelty to daily tooling, with Claude Code, Aider, Cline, OpenHands and Block's Goose all competing for the same developer workflow. The bottleneck is no longer raw model quality but the economics of long autonomous runs: every turn resends context, and any change to the prompt prefix invalidates the provider's cache, multiplying cost and latency. DeepSeek's aggressive cache-hit pricing makes prefix stability unusually valuable, yet most agents mutate context freely (reordering tools, injecting timestamps, dumping stale tool output). Meanwhile MCP standardized tool supply and Zed's Agent Client Protocol (ACP) standardized editor-to-agent plumbing. Reasonix, from the community group esengine, is a bet that a cache-aware, config-driven Go engine can serve terminal, desktop, browser and editor clients from one local core.
key_points: Cache-first context maintenance is the core design bet. Reasonix injects a small, stable environment summary at startup, snips or prunes stale tool output before summary compaction, and documents its tool schema contract so changes that would break prefix caching show up in regression review. The result is fewer cache misses on long runs.

Everything is declared in reasonix.toml: providers, the agent, enabled tools and plugins. DeepSeek ships as a preset, but any OpenAI-compatible endpoint is a config entry rather than new code. Two models can run together as executor and planner in separate, cache-stable sessions.

One local engine, four entry points. The CLI/TUI, an Electron desktop app, a browser client and a VS Code extension (also on Open VSX for VSCodium and Theia) all talk to the same Reasonix engine over ACP, so sessions, model selection and tool approvals behave consistently.

Long autonomous runs stay auditable. Plan mode, a permissions system, a workspace sandbox and per-turn checkpoints with rewind mean a multi-hour agent run can still be read, interrupted and undone rather than trusted blindly.

Distribution is deliberately frictionless: a CGO_ENABLED=0 static Go binary, npm or Homebrew install, one-command cross-compilation to six darwin/linux/windows amd64/arm64 targets, and code-signed Windows installers via SignPath. Extensibility comes from MCP servers plus Extension Protocol v1 sidecars.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Reasonix is a signal that prompt-cache economics are becoming an architectural constraint, not an afterthought; expect more agents to treat context stability as a first-class design goal and to expose a stable tool-schema contract. For developers, it offers a genuinely portable option: one static binary, config-declared providers, MCP and ACP compatibility, and a VS Code surface without vendor lock-in to a single model. The dual executor/planner pattern also gives a cheap way to trade tokens for planning quality. For regular users, the practical win is cost and predictability, since cache-aware context trimming lowers long-session bills, while checkpoints, sandboxing and permission prompts make leaving an agent running unattended less risky. The counterweight is maturity: Go 1.26+ toolchains and a fast-moving 0.x codebase imply migration work ahead.
report.tools: Worth following alongside Reasonix: Aider and OpenHands for open-source terminal agents, Cline and Continue for editor-native flows, Block's Goose for MCP-centric extensibility, and Zed's Agent Client Protocol spec for editor integration patterns. Anthropic's Model Context Protocol registry supplies pluggable tools, and DeepSeek's API docs explain the cache-hit pricing that motivates this design. Reasonix itself installs via npm i -g reasonix or Homebrew, with source at github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix.
